page: Amazon Web Services r8a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The instance delivers 64 physical cores mapped to 64 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading resource sharing. System memory consists of 512.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI. Networking bandwidth is rated at a 30 Gbps baseline. The configuration excludes local block storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark measurements position the instance in the top tier for compute and memory operations. In synthetic CPU tests, it recorded 231,275.72 in stress-ng multi-core and 29,002.0 in Geekbench multi-core, with single-core Geekbench registering 2,749.0. Uncached memory bandwidth testing showed large-block read transfers reaching 423.16 GB/sec and writes at 211.24 GB/sec. Application testing reflected these hardware attributes with 193.5 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput of 117.71 GB/sec. On CPU-based machine learning inference, prompt processing reached 332.29 tokens per second for a medium 7B parameter model.

The qualitative hardware balance delivers high memory and compute density per instance without CPU thread contention. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates network-attached storage for persistent and temporary data, which relies on the 30 Gbps network connection. The hardware configuration aligns directly with in-memory databases, large caching layers, high-volume ETL processing, large software build farms, and memory-bound transactional databases.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Managed via the Nitro hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated physical cores across 64 vCPUs with 1 thread per core, paired with 512.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 6 GHz. It offers a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes zero discrete GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier CPU and memory capabilities, achieving 193.5 million Redis SET operations per second and 423.16 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth. Hardware extensions include AVX-512 vector support and accelerated cryptographic instructions. With an 8.0 GB per core memory allocation and non-hyperthreaded core layout, the instance delivers high compute and memory density, making it suitable for memory-intensive enterprise databases, in-memory caches, large software build pipelines, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
